title: Budd Johnson's musicianship compared with Lester's
summary: Phillips says Budd Johnson knew harmony and had better range on paper, while Prez simply played changes by ear.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Somebody told me he gave a few tips not only to Ben Webster, but he gave some tips to Prez, too -- just about fingering or something.
Oh, he did? I don't know.
I just heard that. I'm not saying that.
Maybe he did. I don't know. He could have. You never know. At that time, he was a better musician than Prez.
Musically. I don't mean playing. I mean musically. He had better range and all that, you know. He knew harmony. Because Prez didn't even know... I'm just speaking about musicianship on paper.
Technical, yeah. Because, see, Prez was playing changes and things. He said he didn't never know what the hell it was until lately...
